citations.review_text:
I could recommend it on sale for fans of RTS and the Halo universe. Not as fleshed out as some of the all time greats but decent variety of units and missions. I'd recommend checking out series like Command and Conquer, Starcraft, Grey Goo, Dark Reign, War Wind, and Blood & Magic first if you haven't already.

+Visuals
+Variety of settings, key rebinding
+Campaign
+Fully voiced
+RTS gameplay
+Cutscenes, story

-Lacking tooltips
-Some unclear abilities
-Base locations locked/limited
-Lack camera zoom
-Single save only

I REALLY liked it, *but* the inability to zoom the camera, the troop ai's threat range being way too big for them to be easily controlled, and the only options being on-screen troops or ALL troops make it a pass for me. I'll probably pick it up again in the future but I'm not entirely invested with those things. Maybe these are just holdovers from it being a console port?

Halo Wars is the game Halo: Combat Evolved was originally planned to be, and then somebody decided that an RTS wasn't the greatest title release to reach a wide audience. As a result it was another console generation before this one came out, and for those of us inclined to this genre it's a bit of an oddity in terms of mechanics and gameplay.

Unlike most RTS build-harvest-train-smash approaches, HW uses an odd system with predefined bases that fit within a given footprint and must be upgraded. Resource gathering is largely a matter of time and upgrading the right building, with barrels of raw material spattered about the landscape to incentivize expansion. It's more or less impossible to use the turtle strategy, so much like Dawn of War it's either expand or expire. This provides fast gameplay but takes away building options which are typical of RTS titles.

With only two factions built in, and mods that allow for a third (the Flood), each faction has a choice of 3 "heroes" that determine what ultimate unit and unique ability you can deploy. The human side leans heavily into mechanized infantry, where the Covenant has an odd mix of heavy vehicles and disposable fodder useful mostly for swarm attacks.

It's an oddball of the genre and one should keep in mind that this is not Halo: Dawn of War by any stretch of the imagination. The map sizes are fairly limited, and the base model is much like DoW 2 in that you use a central base and have little in the way of placement choices in skirmish mode. 

The action in HW hits fast and hard, with little time available to build up assets and deploy them in a meaningful way. You need to jump on your production as fast as possible, espeically as the human faction, or face a rapid depantsing at the hands of cheap and fast suicide grunts. I found it a bit of a challenge to adapt to the somewhat unique mechanics and would strongly recoommend the camera mod as the view is limited at best and the pan/zoom controls are odd. Th…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game mechanics and strategy as heavily simplified compared to other real-time strategy titles, relying largely on massing units into a single group.

citations.review_text:
Calling this baby's first RTS is a disservice to all of the RTS games I played when in my single digits...

Like, I was around when Command and Conquer first dropped. I was alive for when Starcraft and Warcraft 3 came out. I don't say that to flex. I don't say that because I think they're goated, I don't even think that.

Yet, all of those have a little more going on strategically than slamming your deathblob against the enemy deathblob. It's so simplified that it isn't even engaging. The closest thing to strategy is to just pick what makes up your deathblob and, if it doesn't quite work out, alter the make up of said deathblob.

Controlling your army is the biggest challenge the game has to offer. I don't even understand how my air units need to do-si-do around a base that doesn't even exist...plus it feels like every command freezes your units in place for a moment, just what you want when AOE moves get pulled out...

The story is...well, simple. It's a watered down Halo, but like, the "meme" understanding of "Halo." OMG! Aliens are attacking. Oh no, ancient artifacts! Oh dear, me...Flood! Uh oh, something the Forerunners made will be used to kill humanity, let's stopp itt! It's...adequate in the way gruel is adequate...it fills a hole, if only just.

Then, gameplay wise, well...you only really have two factions, humans vs. aliens, with three sub-armies in each. So how do you still have such balance issues? Like, if a smart Covie gets a Scarab on the field you're in trouble. Same with the Prophet hero, whose special ability calls a resource fueled death ray from above. Plus the irksome nature of the Arbiter just jumping on your vehicles and deleting them...

I'm sensing a bias...

It's unbalanced and dull. I don't hate it...indeed I respect it's authenticity to "Halo" as a property. I respect it's attempt at making console RTSes a "thing." Yet, it doesn't really scratch that whole "strategy" itch, so I can't recommend it.

The Legendary Bald Space Marine

Halo Wars is a game about how to strategic eliminate your enemy, by pumping out units and overwhelming them, while a bald man is having a generic action adventure.

it's a fine strategy game that becomes amazing, if you play it in Co-op, where you can give units to your friend and divide jobs between you. When playing on PC it is a bit of an easier time, because you have so much more individual control of your unit, that you ever had on Xbox 360.

The missions  varied are good, give you different challenges throughout the game.micromanaging you have with the unit, where you have to press the special attack button, to get as much out of a possible are good.

they is a Problem of giving you 3 overpowered spartans, that can resurrect themselves, the difficulty kind of dies if you're not playing on legendary.

The story is a really dumb action version of what a normal Halo game is, but just without any of the AW,  we do have bold spaceman who can show us a way, and sassy Ai that is not katana.

As a person who's only interested in campaigns and not interested in multiplayers. It's a good time, but you need friendship to really appreciate it alone. I would not give it a second glands.

I liked it, very fun RTS game. Not as deep as something like warcraft which I grew up with but very enjoyable and beginner friendly because of how simple it is, though I did wish it was a bit deeper. I also wish the missions were longer but that goes to show how fun this game is, I may get alot of hate but the gameplay of this game was better than actual halo games. The story is also pretty engaging but its not something I would remember, in fact I just beat the game and I already forgot. Halo wars 2 isn't on steam unfortunately but that won't stop me, I had a lot of fun here so I'll get my hands on Halo wars 2 right now.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC port features awkward controls and a clunky user interface.

citations.review_text:
I originally played this game on the Xbox 360 and I remember having a good time yet I never returned to it. Replaying it on PC, I find it to be a rather miserable experience, in no minor part due to the console origin of the title.  I don't care for the multiplayer so everything I write here is about the singleplayer campaign. 

The developers did the bare minimum in adapting the game for the PC. The controls are awful, the user interface is awful. The minimap is nearly useless for locating your troops - at best you can identify enemy units but good luck finding your own. In the chaos of a mission, I do not have time to struggle with finding my hero units. The grouping system is fine but doesn't solve the problem.

The basebuilding and the units are alright. You harvest resources through a specialized building or by finding them on the map, build barracks and buy upgrades. You build dedicated anti-infantry units, anti-vechicle units, anti-air units etc, the standard stuff, and every unit has unique abilities. You also have leader abilities like MAC strikes. It's what you would expect from an RTS. 
I can't say the AI is clever - from what I can tell, they simply have unlimited resources and you don't, so you have to learn by trial and error and restart missions if you didn't already know what was in store for you. For example, in a mission you can scout out locations where you need to place special vehicles. I had my epicsauce Spartans in one location while a vehicle got in position at another spot - this suddenly triggered an event where an enemy base spawned on top of my Spartans and they were quickly war crime'd. Time for a reload! Not exactly stellar game design and since you can't skip the in-game cutscenes, you're forced to rewatch the same stuff every time you want to replay a mission. There is thankfully an in-mission save system but it is limited to one save slot - another remnant of the console past, I imagine. I will give the game credit though - the anima…
Very clunky, and the UI could be better. However overall a good game, very graphically pleasing especially if you like Halo because this RTS leans into Halo realism.

Was released in 2009 for the Xbox 360 by a studio mistreated by both Microsoft and Bungie. Don't expect a heavily polished PC RTS like Supreme Commander FA, StarCraft, or Dawn of War. It's got a lot of jank and controls aren't up to standards with other RTS games but It makes sense though, the game wasn't developed with MnK in mind but just controller. 

I still recommended this game even with it's problems, the game has a very talented modding community that has been able to create their very own mod tools and very soon map editor with no support from 343 Industries/Halo Studios. The campaign isn't perfect but it's really enjoyable. A lot of this is also nostalgia talking as I have very fond memories of staying up all night and playing 3v3s with my friends. I hope someday we get a Steam release for Halo Wars 2 and eventually a Halo Wars 3.

claims.claim: Resource gathering is largely automatic through production buildings rather than requiring traditional economic micro-management.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Halo Wars: Definitive Edition[/h1]
[h3]Great Straightforward RTS[/h3]
[h3]Really worth trying for fans of the strategy genre and Halo[/h3]

Halo Wars is a very original spin-off from the modern golden age of the RTS genre. It’s a pretty unique and creative title for a franchise that has always been known for its excellent sci-fi first-person shooters entries. Personally, I think it’s a great RTS on its own, even without necessarily relying on the Halo franchise, since its gameplay is really fun, it has an engaging campaign and solid strategy mechanics overall.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
Halo Wars has a more simplified game design compared to other strategy games from its era. Still, it keeps the essential strategy mechanics like resource management, economy and army management. Adding to that, resource gathering in this game is mostly automatic, since it relies on production buildings that generate resources over time, which changes the classic economic micro management found in other RTS games. Personally, I’ve always preferred this kind of system, since it allows for more focus on the action and strategic decision-making.

On the other hand, the strategic combat system is pretty well-balanced, with clear counters for infantry and vehicles, units that have specific roles and oversimplified controls that make the game easy to manage. However, it’s true that the lack of advanced commands can make the game feel a bit limited in terms of strategic movements such as specific unit formations.

I must mention that there are only two factions available: the UNSC and the Covenant. Each one has three commanders to choose from, each with unique units and abilities. Honestly, the lack of variety in factions can actually make the game feel a bit repetitive, especially in skirmish matches and multiplayer. Nevertheless, the gameplay is still very enjoyable and becomes more engaging as the game progress.

[h3]Art and World Design[/h3]
This game has a really appealing cinematic visual …

Halo Wars is a brilliant twist on the Halo franchise, bringing real-time strategy (RTS) gameplay to the iconic universe of Master Chief and the Covenant. Developed by Ensemble Studios and released for Xbox 360, it was a bold departure from the traditional first-person shooter formula. However, it proved that the Halo universe could expand into new genres and still deliver an exciting, immersive experience.

One of the things that stands out the most about Halo Wars is how it successfully translates the fast-paced action of Halo into a strategic, tactical format. The game takes place before the events of the main Halo games, focusing on the story of the UNSC’s efforts to fight the Covenant and uncover mysterious forces threatening humanity. The plot is engaging, offering a fresh perspective on the war between the Covenant and the humans, and it adds depth to the lore of the series.

The gameplay is incredibly accessible, especially for players who might not be familiar with RTS games. The controls are intuitive, especially for a console RTS, and the game’s streamlined mechanics allow for fast-paced combat without being overwhelming. Despite its simplification compared to traditional PC RTS titles, Halo Wars still offers plenty of strategic depth. The player has to manage resources, command units, and make quick tactical decisions on the battlefield, all while balancing offensive and defensive strategies.

The game’s visual presentation is top-notch, with stunning representations of Halo’s iconic vehicles and characters. The beautifully crafted environments, from the lush alien landscapes to the massive spaceships, really bring the world of Halo to life in a way that feels unique to the RTS genre. The cutscenes are cinematic and well-directed, which further draws you into the experience.

Halo Wars also features an engaging multiplayer component, offering competitive and co-op gameplay. The multiplayer is a blast, allowing players to face off in fast-paced strategy ba…

citations.review_text:
Halo Wars is probably one of the most underrated Halo games ever made.

Taking Halo and turning it into an RTS sounds like something that shouldn't have worked anywhere near as well as it did, but somehow it just works.

Building up your base, getting a massive army together and sending 20 Scorpions across the map to absolutely delete someone's base never gets old.

The campaign is great as well. The story actually feels like Halo, the cutscenes are brilliant and the Spirit of Fire crew are genuinely some of my favourite characters in the entire series.

And for an RTS that was made around playing on a controller, the controls are surprisingly good.

Obviously its not perfect.

The AI can sometimes have absolutely no idea what its doing, units get stuck on each other, pathfinding can be questionable and trying to get a specific group of units to go exactly where you want can turn into its own mission.

It's also definitely simpler than a lot of other RTS games. If you've spent your entire life playing StarCraft you're probably not going to find Halo Wars particularly complicated.

But honestly thats part of why I like it.

You don't need a university degree in resource management just to understand what's happening. You build your base, make an army and go blow up the other bloke.

Simple.

The multiplayer was also some of the most fun I've had in a strategy game, especially when everyone stops pretending they're using tactics and just starts building the most ridiculous army possible.

Halo Wars isn't the deepest RTS ever made.

It isn't the most complicated.

But its fun as ♥♥♥♥.

Great campaign.

Great soundtrack.

Great atmosphere.

And nothing will ever beat hearing:

"ALL UNITS"

for the 400th time.

One of my favorite Halo games, grew up with this one and Reach.

I've been exploring modding with it recently, my only concerns is the AI has a potato brain and may or may not do something stupid and follow the same path, 5 matches in a row.

A fairly simple RTS even for its day, but it's charming in its simplicity and pretty addictive to boot, it doesn't feel shallow or unfinished at all. Artistically it's extremely faithful to the feel of the original Halo games (back then they were the only Halo games lol) in visuals, sounds, and overall tone/mood. The PC port is also a little better than the original version I remember playing so many years ago, they added some new hotkeys (including control groups) and slightly improved the graphics.

I especially love the skulls and alternative gamemodes, not a lot of RTS games go beyond the basic KOTH/annihilation gamemodes and not a lot of games in general have quirky difficulty modifiers. My favourite game type is Reinforcement where your resources are consumed automatically every minute (on average, there's some random variation) in exchange for a random assortment of units.

Even as an RTS veteran, I find Halo Wars to be a nice break from other games because its simplicity makes it so easy to pick up. It makes a good depression game in that respect, doesn't take much energy to get started here.

Also, being able to see where your allies are looking on the minimap is a nice quality of life feature that I wish was in other strategy games.

Halo Wars is probably one of the most underrated Halo games ever made.

Taking Halo and turning it into an RTS sounds like something that shouldn't have worked anywhere near as well as it did, but somehow it just works.

Building up your base, getting a massive army together and sending 20 Scorpions across the map to absolutely delete someone's base never gets old.

The campaign is great as well. The story actually feels like Halo, the cutscenes are brilliant and the Spirit of Fire crew are genuinely some of my favourite characters in the entire series.

And for an RTS that was made around playing on a controller, the controls are surprisingly good.

Obviously its not perfect.

The AI can sometimes have absolutely no idea what its doing, units get stuck on each other, pathfinding can be questionable and trying to get a specific group of units to go exactly where you want can turn into its own mission.

It's also definitely simpler than a lot of other RTS games. If you've spent your entire life playing StarCraft you're probably not going to find Halo Wars particularly complicated.

But honestly thats part of why I like it.

You don't need a university degree in resource management just to understand what's happening. You build your base, make an army and go blow up the other bloke.

Simple.

The multiplayer was also some of the most fun I've had in a strategy game, especially when everyone stops pretending they're using tactics and just starts building the most ridiculous army possible.

Halo Wars isn't the deepest RTS ever made.

It isn't the most complicated.

But its fun as ♥♥♥♥.

Great campaign.

Great soundtrack.

Great atmosphere.

And nothing will ever beat hearing:

"ALL UNITS"

for the 400th time.

One of my favorite Halo games, grew up with this one and Reach.

I've been exploring modding with it recently, my only concerns is the AI has a potato brain and may or may not do something stupid and follow the same path, 5 matches in a row.
